## Overview

A category groups product pages that share a supply chain and a regulatory posture, so that evidence which applies to the whole group is stated once rather than repeated on every page beneath it. The Index tracks 34 categories covering 357 subcategory pages. Start here when a question is about a kind of product rather than about one specific item; start at the metal or the ingredient when it is about a contaminant or a raw material.

## How categories are built

Category membership comes from each product page's own declared taxonomy, not from an editorial list kept alongside it, so a page joins or leaves a category by changing its own frontmatter and the grouping cannot drift from the pages it describes. Counts on this page are the number of subcategory pages currently routed to each category; they are a measure of coverage in the corpus, not of how many products exist in the market. A category with few pages means the reading is thin there, not that the category is small.
